title: Signature Levenshtein edit distance — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — Levenshtein distance counts the minimum insertions, deletions, and substitutions turning one string into another. The classic dynamic program fills an (m+1)x(n+1) table where each cell takes the minimum of its three neighbors plus a substitution cost. Distance 1 or 2 captures the vast majority of human typos, which is why it anchors typo-tolerant search. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
demo:
# Typo-tolerant search: Levenshtein distance suggests corrections within a budget.
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = list(range(len(b) + 1))
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
words = ['archive','archival','archives','index']
query = "archvie"
budget = 2
cands = sorted(((levenshtein(query, w), w) for w in words if levenshtein(query, w) <= budget))
print(f"Query {query!r}, max distance {budget}:")
for d, w in cands:
    print(f"  {w!r} (distance {d})")
if not cands: print("  no candidates within budget")
provenance: Signature-authored original method created for the JAH archive toolkit; clearly labeled Signature, not a public record.

title: Signature Damerau-Levenshtein with transpositions — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — Adjacent transpositions ('teh' for 'the') are the most common typo, so Damerau-Levenshtein counts a swap as one edit. The extended recurrence tracks the last row each character appeared in, adding the transposition option. With transpositions, 'recieve' sits at distance 1 from 'receive' instead of 2. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Keyboard-adjacency weighting — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — Not all substitutions are equal: 'q' for 'w' is a near-miss on QWERTY while 'q' for 'p' is not. Weighted edit distance scales substitution cost by physical key distance. Keyboard-aware costs rank the plausible typo above the coincidence. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature N-gram similarity — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — Character n-grams (usually trigrams) turn strings into sets; similarity is the overlap of those sets. 'archive' and 'archvie' share most trigrams despite the transposition, giving high Jaccard similarity. N-gram indexes also enable fast candidate generation before exact distance checks. title: Signature SymSpell deletion index — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — SymSpell precomputes every string within k deletions of each vocabulary term and indexes those deletes. A query's own deletes then hit the index directly, finding candidates without scanning the vocabulary. Lookup is effectively constant time, which is why SymSpell powers real-time correction. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature BK-tree nearest neighbors — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — A BK-tree organizes the vocabulary by edit distance from chosen pivots, pruning whole subtrees during search. Querying walks only branches whose pivot distance falls within [d-k, d+k] of the query. BK-trees answer nearest-neighbor typo queries in sublinear time on large lexicons. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Levenshtein automata — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — A Levenshtein automaton for a query and budget k accepts exactly the strings within distance k. Walking it alongside a trie finds all vocabulary matches in time proportional to matches, not vocabulary size. Automata-based fuzzy search is how databases implement efficient 'LIKE with typos'. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Noisy-channel spelling correction — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — The noisy-channel model picks the correction c maximizing P(c) * P(query|c): language prior times error likelihood. P(c) comes from word frequencies; P(query|c) from confusion matrices of real typo corpora. This ranks 'the' above 'teh'-neighbors correctly because 'the' is far more probable. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Setting the distance budget — Typographical Error Search
description: Signature original — Budget k=1 is nearly always safe; k=2 helps short queries but risks false friends on long vocabularies. Adaptive budgets scale with query length, often floor(len/4), keeping precision stable. Tuning k on labeled typo pairs beats any fixed rule.
